subject: Service routing briefing - recommended customer actions for regional cloud disruption
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@acme-payments.com>, Platform Ops (Acme Payments) <platformops@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Immediate actions: partial regional outage and recommended traffic reroute

Hi Maya —

Quick note to confirm we observed a partial outage impacting Redwood-hosted inference nodes in the eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 cloud regions starting ~07:40 UTC. US regions (us-east-1, us-west-2) are operating normally. We are actively engaging the cloud provider and our routing subsystems.

For Acme Payments specifically: to minimize user-facing latency and reduce error rates, please consider the following immediate options (we can apply any or all on your behalf if you prefer):

- Temporary region pin: Route all inference traffic to us-east-1. This avoids eu/apac regional queues. Expected impact: small latency increase for EU/APAC end-users but improved success rate.
- Graceful degradation: Use cached embeddings for non-critical recommendation flows for 20 minutes to avoid token generation failures.
- Failover header: Add X-Redwood-Failover: true to retry logic so our client routing can prefer dedicated capacity if your account is eligible.

We've attached a short "reroute-playbook.pdf" (staged runbook) with step-by-step commands and the estimated cost delta for region pinning. If you'd like us to enact the pin now, reply with the preferred target region (us-east-1 or us-west-2) and an explicit ack to proceed.

Apologies for the disruption — we will keep you updated every 60 minutes or sooner with material changes.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: reroute-playbook.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-21T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate actions: partial regional outage and recommended traffic reroute

On Thu, Jun 21, 2028 at 08:12 Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick note to confirm we observed a partial outage impacting Redwood-hosted inference nodes in the eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 cloud regions starting ~07:40 UTC.

We have confirmed elevated 5xxs and connection timeouts to the router mesh for those regions. Network team reports provider-mapped maintenance + an unexpected control-plane thrash.

Recommended immediate course (in priority order):
1) Apply account-level region pin to us-east-1 for Acme Payments (low risk).
2) Activate prefix KV caching for their high-volume endpoints (reduces token spend and retries).
3) Enable short-lived client-side fallback to the hosted API with X-Redwood-Failover header.

I can enact 1 and 2 for Acme once we have Acme ops ack. I'll also drop a CSV with current latency/error metrics to the thread.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE, Runtime Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Maya —

Thanks for the quick ack. We'll:
- Apply account-level pin to us-east-1 (target start 09:15 PDT).
- Enable prefix KV caching for Acme's high-volume endpoints immediately.
- Provide a short status blurb below for your status page and a one-click acknowledgement template attachment.

We will confirm when the pin is in place and share the initial success metrics.

— Naomi

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@acme-payments.com>, Platform Ops (Acme Payments) <platformops@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary & next steps — regional router disruption (eu/apac)

Hi Maya —

Summary (impact window): 07:40 UTC 2028-06-21 to 10:30 UTC 2028-06-21. Root cause: cloud provider control-plane maintenance that overlapped with an unannounced routing table refresh, causing transient mesh reconfiguration and elevated connection errors in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1.

What we did for Acme:
- Applied account pinning to us-east-1 at 09:18 PDT (reduced errors immediately).
- Enabled prefix KV caching for high-volume endpoints (reduced token usage and retries).
- Monitored for 18 hours and confirmed stable behaviour; we reverted the manual pin at 04:00 PDT on 2028-06-22 and traffic gradually moved back over 40 minutes.

Customer-facing impact: No payment routing failures attributable to Redwood were observed during the pin window; the customer-reported incidents were resolved after the pin. We captured detailed latency/error timelines in the attached CSV.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- SRE: negotiate provider SLA credit and log provider ticket (Marcus) / ETA 2028-06-24.
- Product: add an automated account-level failover toggle in Console (Jonas) / ETA roadmap Q4 2028.
- CS/AM: run a short review with Acme to confirm cost delta and any billing offsets (Naomi) / ETA 2028-06-25.

We're attaching the reroute playbook and the latency metrics. If you want a consolidated incident report in your vendor compliance format (SOC2-ready) let us know and we'll add the extra detail.

Again, sorry for the interruption. Happy to jump on a quick call if you want a walkthrough.

— Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: reroute-playbook.pdf, latency-metrics-20280621.csv
